note: WRITE A MERGE HEADLINE WITHOUT A merge() PREFIX — THE CHAMBER SUPPLIES ONE. sluice-run.sh composes the merge commit subject as merge(branch-leaf) colon space, then the candidate tip subject, verbatim. It ALWAYS prefixes. The Rhumb wrote a tip subject that already read merge(the-rhumb) colon ... because that is how a merge headline should read, and landed on main as merge(the-rhumb): merge(the-rhumb): the compass now means what it says, and one bound that did not. Doubled, cosmetic, and permanent — history is not retroactively fixable. Merge commit 9aae0d27, main c25cf53a. The queue operator states the defect is in what it advised rather than in what the campaign wrote, and has the strip-the-prefix fix scheduled with a test. UNTIL THAT LANDS: write the tip subject as the summary ALONE, no merge() wrapper. THIS IS THE THIRD WAY THE HEADLINE MECHANISM BIT IN ONE EVENING, which is the finding rather than any single instance. One: displaced by a later commit, The Begat, twice, the second time after knowing about it, because a docs commit added afterwards silently pushed the fixed headline off the tip. Two: unfit for purpose at the tip, a wip-style subject about to become permanent. Three: doubled by a prefix nobody was told about. All three close the same way — take the headline from a DESIGNATED PLACE rather than inferring it from whichever commit happens to be last. A position is not a name. SECOND FACT, useful separately: a merge commit subject becomes a CENSUS EPOCH LABEL only if the merge moves book/src/laboratory/generated/the-census/rows.csv, because tools/census/history.sh is path-scoped and first-parent over that one file. The Rhumb moved no census, so it minted no epoch. The subject is still permanent and human-read either way.
